title: Fix the five newcomer findings on the Athena explainer page
summary: The page is generated by xtask/src/site.rs from studies/firstmate-work-handling/*.json. The reading edits the intro text and the renderer so a newcomer meets Athena before firstmate, the study id is explained, the five terms are defined or linked on first use, f2 is rewritten, and the Counters entry says which transitions take and free a place, with links to the transition cards. The audience is a first-time visitor to doodla.github.io/athena. The final report must hold the finding-to-HTML table and the gate results.

defaults_applied.how: The renderer change comes with site.rs tests, and cargo test and clippy must be clean.
Criteria check the built HTML text and links, not that files exist.
The page text is written for a first-time reader.
New factual statements about firstmate cite claim ids, as the renderer requires.
I recovered the page's source files from the repository instead of asking.
One focused change that touches the page text and its renderer.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: I chose to add an Athena introduction and keep the study on the front page, which is the less disruptive of the two options in finding 1.

The sentence 'a place is freed only when a worker records its ready PR or is cleaned up' maps to t3 (ready PR) and t4 (cleanup). This is taken from the intro text and the counter's changed_by list [t1,t3,t4]. The producer should confirm it against claim c3 and the transition data.

Definitions of home, scout, endpoint, secondmate and brief are written from the cited claims or sources in claims.json. Any definition that no claim supports links to the glossary and is marked as being about the page.
The rating of 2026-10-15T14:57 is not in the repository. Findings are taken from the request wording.
Page text lives in the study JSON files and is rendered from them, so edits go there. The renderer changes only for anchors, links and first-use handling.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site` (or the repo's site-build command, with output outside the work tree) and read the front-page HTML. Before the firstmate study text, it has at least a short passage saying what Athena is, how it works, and why this study exists. Alternatively the study is moved off the front page, and the front page links to it.
In the built HTML the study id 'firstmate-work-handling' is explained in plain words where it first appears, as the name of the study of firstmate at a pinned commit.

In the built HTML each of home, scout, endpoint, secondmate and brief has an inline definition at its first appearance, or links to a glossary entry. The glossary has an entry for each, and each link target id exists in the HTML.

The built HTML no longer contains the old f2 text ('The study's data format asks every guard to name who checks it'). Any f2 note that remains is plain prose that a reader without the study format can follow.

In the built HTML the Counters entry for places-held says that t1 takes a place and that t3 and t4 free one. Each of t1, t3 and t4 is an <a href="#..."> whose target id is on the matching transition card.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, and `cargo test` all pass. The tests include new or updated site.rs tests covering the transition links and the first-use definitions.
The final report has a table with one row per finding (1 to 5). Each row has an HTML excerpt taken from the built page, and the report lists the gate commands with their results.

out_of_scope: Changes to the study's claims, pin or validation of the studied firstmate content.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows.
Redesigning the page layout or styling beyond what the five findings need.
departures: Slightly above the reference: five findings, a renderer change with tests, and a report table.
